item.title: Euronews: Humanoid robots: China builds them, but Germany could supply the joints and hands
item.description: Europe has so far built few humanoid robots, yet could profit from each one. German car part suppliers may play a key role in joints, says a Fraunhofer study.

item.description: Passengers on a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight recount the terrifying moments after an altercation erupted in the cockpit. As the plane was diverted to Saudi Arabia, passengers say several people rushed to intervene and helped bring the situation under control.

item.title: Euronews: Protests continue at French schools as tensions rise over education conditions
item.description: Students continued to protest at schools in France, demanding more resources and better learning conditions, while tensions and vandalism were reported around several schools in Rennes.

item.title: Euronews: Swiss glaciers lose 5.5% of ice in second-largest melt on record
item.description: Swiss scientists report rapid ice loss at the Rhône Glacier, as heatwaves and a dry winter drive Switzerland’s second-biggest melt on record.

item.title: Euronews: Kanye West’s controversial concerts in Russia have finally been cancelled
item.description: According to the Moscow-based organizer Say Agency, the controversial rapper's two October dates in St Petersburg have been cancelled. Russian media states that the decision was made by the authorities, who are reportedly investigating the organizers for alleged fraud.

item.title: Euronews: Can Canada be the EU's answer to 'unreliable' trade partners?
item.description: Ahead of October's EU-Canada summit, both sides are considering a partnership beyond CETA and €130 billion in annual trade. Nothing is agreed on financial services, and the new "associate member" tier has no legal definition.

item.title: Euronews: Rutte responds to Moscow's nuclear threats, and the UK leader weighs re-joining the EU
item.description: Good morning, I’m Mared Gwyn. Welcome to your Thursday newsletter. Today: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte tells Euronews that Russia should stop issuing nuclear threats, and the UK Prime Minister puts EU membership back on the table.

item.title: Euronews: Before the Iran war vs now: How much of a worker’s wage is needed to fill a 50-litre tank?
item.description: A 50-litre diesel tank costs the equivalent of 15.4% of Bulgaria’s gross monthly minimum wage, compared with 3.8% in Luxembourg, as fuel prices have risen since the Iran war began.

item.title: Euronews: “I grabbed the controls”: FlyDubai survivor recounts dramatic cockpit attack as he meets Netanyahu
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met Yaniv Hayun, one of the passengers who helped subdue a pilot after a stabbing on a Flydubai flight bound for Israel.

item.title: Euronews: Europe Today: Rutte tells Russia to stop nuclear threats at Euronews defence summit
item.description: NATO chief Mark Rutte tells Russia to stop its nuclear threats, speaking at the Euronews Defence Summit as Moscow threatens to use its nuclear arsenal. Rutte also said there's no imminent threat to NATO territory, while Belgian defence chief Theo Francken argued Russia is Belgium's biggest threat.

item.description: Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend beat and killed Colleen Slemmer, 19, at a job training camp for young people.

item.description: The Colombian pop star returns to Spain after eight years with a 12-show residency in Madrid, celebrating Latin culture and turning a chapter of her life into a spectacle of music, freedom and empowerment.

item.title: Euronews: Hundreds held, dozens wounded as protests over conditions in French schools escalate

item.title: Euronews: Where does body fat go when we lose weight? The answer is stranger than you expect
